claims.text: Aging Al0.7CoCrFeNi at 550–600 °C for 1–2 hours will precipitate fine, coherent L12 particles within the fcc lamellae.
The specified aging treatment will simultaneously increase yield strength and ductility relative to the as-cast alloy.
As-cast Al0.7CoCrFeNi has a lamellar microstructure containing coexisting fcc and B2 phases.
The as-cast alloy contains no significant L12 precipitate population.
Post-casting homogenization is required to ensure chemical uniformity before aging.
Tight control of aging temperature and time is required to prevent overaging and precipitate coarsening.
Using an inert atmosphere or vacuum during aging will minimize oxidation.
The aging treatment will produce a uniform dispersion of fine, coherent L12 nanoprecipitates in the fcc lamellae.
L12 nanoprecipitates obstruct dislocation motion through Orowan bowing and bypass, thereby increasing yield strength.
Coherence between the L12 precipitates and the fcc matrix maintains deformation compatibility.
The coherent L12 precipitates induce back-stress strengthening.
Back-stress strengthening enhances work hardening and consequently improves ductility.
The specified aging treatment will increase yield strength by approximately 20–30% relative to the as-cast alloy.
The aged alloy will retain or slightly improve ductility because of increased strain-hardening capacity.
The beneficial response is restricted to aging at 550–600 °C for 1–2 hours.
Longer aging times or higher temperatures may coarsen the precipitates and embrittle the alloy.
Minor compositional fluctuations and heat-treatment variations can alter precipitate distribution and mechanical performance.

contradictions.description: The conditions require post-casting homogenization before aging, but the baseline is explicitly as-cast and the experimental design does not specify homogenizing either the aged specimens or a matched control. Comparing homogenized-and-aged material with an as-cast control would change more than the aging intervention and confound the result.
